abstract: Abstract Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning (QML) relies on Quantum Variational Circuits (QVCs) trained together with classical components. While gradient-based training is standard, it is costly on near-term hardware and vulnerable to barren plateaus, motivating gradient-free alternatives. However, there is limited systematic evidence comparing gradient-free methods to strong gradient baselines under matched quantum-evaluation budgets. A benchmark of 14 gradient-based, gradient-free, and hybrid optimizers is conducted on four binary classification datasets and two three-qubit QVC architectures using a unified TensorFlow/PennyLane implementation with a fixed per-step quantum-evaluation budget. Across tasks, Adam is the strongest gradient-based method. Among the purely gradient-free schemes, the Asexual Reproductive Algorithm is the strongest optimizer; tournament-selection and elite-pool genetic algorithms (GA-Tourn, GA-Elite) also frequently match the best gradient-based configurations. Among the hybrid schemes, Gradient Lexicase Selection Adam (GLS-Adam) performs comparably. In contrast, the two gradient-free methods Big Bang-Big Crunch and a Cross-Entropy Method variant often fail to improve beyond chance. Overall, gradient-based methods remain robust defaults for hybrid QML, while a small subset of gradient-free and hybrid approaches provides viable alternatives under realistic quantum-evaluation constraints.
title: Gradient-based versus gradient-free optimization in hybrid quantum machine learning: a systematic benchmark

abstract: Spatial-light computing requires rewritable, multilevel and persistent optical weights, but many implementations rely on volatile modulators or static power. Here we report a CMOS-imaged luminescent memristor array in which ferroelectric domain switching in Er/Yb-doped PMN-PT single crystals programs non-volatile photoluminescence (PL) states. Domain reconfiguration tunes the local crystal-field symmetry of lanthanide emitters, enabling 16 analogue levels, retention over 27 h, endurance beyond 105 cycles and microsecond-scale state programming with zero electrical standby power for state retention. An 8 × 8 array, addressed by a diffractive optical element and read by a proximal CMOS sensor, converts stored emissive states into a single-frame intensity map and achieves 94.02% pixel-wise state recognition using calibration-aware decoding. The array implements single-step optical linear weighting, while the same decoded weights support hybrid optical-electrical handwritten-digit inference approaching a 32-bit floating-point software baseline. These results establish a non-volatile, image-addressable emissive weight element for photonic computing. Spatial-light computing is limited by the lack of compact, non-volatile, rewritable analog devices. Wen et al. report a ferroelectric crystal that converts lanthanide emission into a rewritable, multilevel memory, allowing stored optical states to be read and used as persistent weights for neuromorphic computing.
title: Ferroelectrically programmable lanthanide luminescent memristor
